package_info.package_versions: All UI builds deployed to IPFS since January 1, 2024
package_info.why_malicious: A developer inserted malicious JavaScript into the Tornado Cash user interface, which covertly exfiltrated users’ private deposit notes to an attacker-controlled server, enabling theft of funds. This was a supply chain attack hidden in a governance proposal, targeting users accessing the UI via IPFS gateways.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (user interaction with Tornado Cash UI functions)
execution_context.file_location: JavaScript source code of the Tornado Cash web UI (deployed on IPFS gateways)
required_permissions: access to in-memory deposit notes/private keys

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code captures the user's private deposit note when they interact with the UI, encodes it, and sends it via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled server, enabling secret exfiltration of credentials.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates sensitive cryptographic material (deposit notes) to an external server without user consent or legitimate purpose.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Tornado Cash UI code should never transmit private deposit notes or keys off-device; all cryptographic operations should remain local and private.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or telemetry might send non-sensitive usage data, but never private keys or deposit notes.
key_indicators: Access to sensitive in-memory cryptographic material
Network request to untrusted, hardcoded external domain
Encoding and transmission of user secrets

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is inserted into the Tornado Cash UI codebase via a deceptive developer contribution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Deployment of compromised UI to IPFS gateways

attack_chain.action: Users access the compromised Tornado Cash UI via IPFS gateways (e.g., ipfs.io, cf-ipfs.com).
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code in users' browsers

attack_chain.action: When users interact with the UI (e.g., deposit/withdraw), the malicious code captures their private deposit notes.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of deposit notes to attacker

attack_chain.action: Attacker receives deposit notes and uses them to access and steal users' funds from Tornado Cash.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code accessing deposit notes or private keys in memory
Network requests from the UI to non-Tornado Cash, hardcoded external domains
Encoding and exfiltration of sensitive user data during normal UI operations
file_indicators: Unexpected JavaScript code in Tornado Cash UI source referencing external domains
Obfuscated or hidden code blocks in governance proposal merges
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests from user browsers to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., https://attacker-server.com/collect)
Outbound connections from IPFS-hosted Tornado Cash UI to unknown endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Tornado Cash UI JavaScript for any code that accesses deposit notes or private keys and sends them to external domains. Use browser/network monitoring to detect POST requests to non-official endpoints during user interaction. Audit all code contributions, especially those merged via governance proposals, for hidden or obfuscated network exfiltration logic.
